quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #11
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: If a driver is worried, nervous, angry, or crying, they should:

options.text: Drive the same way they normally would.
Drive faster because they are more alert.
Calm down and focus before starting the car.
Call a friend to talk while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Calm down and focus before starting the car.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions like worry, anger, or sadness can distract you from driving. Your mind focuses on the emotion instead of the road. Always calm down and get focused before you drive.

questions.question: What does this black and yellow sign mean?

options.text: The road to the right is one-way traffic only.
There is a detour to the right due to roadwork.
Slow down because the road ahead curves sharply.
There is a crossroad to your right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down because the road ahead curves sharply.
questions.explanation: This sign means the road ahead curves sharply in one direction. Slow down before you reach a sharp curve, just as you would at an intersection turn.

questions.question: When driving on an interstate, you should:

options.text: Stop on the shoulder if you are tired.
Always use cruise control.
Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
Change lanes often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Always signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot before you change lanes or pass. Only stop on the shoulder in an emergency. Avoid changing lanes often. Do not use cruise control in heavy traffic or bad weather.

questions.question: Many crashes happen because:

options.text: Drivers go too fast for the conditions.
Drivers check their mirrors and blind spots.
Drivers yield the right-of-way.
Drivers keep a four-second following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers go too fast for the conditions.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen when drivers go too fast for road conditions. Always drive at or below the speed limit. Drive slower when conditions are poor.

questions.question: Drinking coffee after drinking alcohol:

options.text: Lowers blood alcohol content.
Stops the effects of alcohol.
Does not change blood alcohol content.
Raises blood alcohol content.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not change blood alcohol content.
questions.explanation: Coffee cannot reduce your blood alcohol content. While coffee may keep you awake, it cannot make you sober or change your blood alcohol level.

questions.question: When a traffic light shows a green arrow and a red light, it means:

options.text: You may only drive straight.
You may only drive in the direction of the green arrow.
You must wait for a solid green light to move in any direction.
All vehicles must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may only drive in the direction of the green arrow.
questions.explanation: A green arrow with a red light means you can only drive in the direction the arrow points. The intersection must be clear before you move.

questions.question: When entering a roadway from a driveway or private road, you should:

options.text: Honk your horn to warn drivers.
Partially drive onto the roadway to alert other drivers.
Drive out fast to merge with traffic smoothly.
Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway.
questions.explanation: When entering a roadway from a driveway or private road, you must yield to pedestrians and all traffic already on the roadway.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on a highway, you should:

options.text: Stay in your car and wait for help.
Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
Honk your horn at passing cars.
Flash your headlights at oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: If your car breaks down on the highway, turn on your hazard flashers. Exit the roadway safely and move far off the road. Lift your hood so other drivers know you need help.

questions.question: On slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Slow down.
Drive faster.
Drive at the speed limit with caution.
Never drive faster than 20 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down when rain, snow, or ice makes the road slippery. When conditions are poor, safety may require you to drive slower than the posted speed limit.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic signal ahead is showing red.
The traffic signal ahead is broken.
The traffic signal ahead is showing green.
There is a traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that there is a traffic signal at the next intersection.

questions.question: What is true about drowsy drivers?

options.text: They should drink strong black coffee to stay awake.
They can drive so poorly that they may look drunk.
They can stay alert by opening a window and turning up the radio.
They are usually only older drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can drive so poorly that they may look drunk.
questions.explanation: Drowsy drivers can perform very poorly, similar to drunk drivers. Coffee, open windows, and loud radio do not keep a drowsy driver alert to road hazards.

questions.question: How does alcohol affect your reflexes and judgment?

options.text: Less when you drink beer instead of wine.
Less when you drink wine instead of beer.
Most when you drink hard ciders and mixed drinks.
It depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.
questions.explanation: All types of alcohol harm your reflexes and judgment. The type of alcohol does not matter. Only the amount of alcohol in your bloodstream affects how impaired you are.

questions.question: Hydroplaning is usually caused by:

options.text: Excessive stops.
Sudden stops.
Sudden turns.
Driving too fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too fast.
questions.explanation: When you drive fast, your tires cannot clear water from the road. They lose grip and slide on a layer of water. This is called hydroplaning.

questions.question: Your blind spot is:

options.text: An area you cannot see without turning your head.
The area directly behind your vehicle.
An area you see in your rearview mirror.
An area you see in your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: An area you cannot see without turning your head.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see without turning your head. They are located to the sides and behind your vehicle.

questions.question: When you see an accident, you should:

options.text: Keep your attention on your driving.
Keep moving.
Stop only if you are involved or emergency help has not arrived.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not stop at an accident unless you are involved or emergency help has not arrived. Stay focused on driving and keep moving. Watch for people on or near the road. Never drive to an accident or disaster just to look.

questions.question: When must drivers yield to a pedestrian?

options.text: Even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.
Only when the pedestrian is in a crosswalk.
Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road.
If the pedestrian uses a hand signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.
questions.explanation: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians in the street. This is true even if they cross against a red light or are being careless.

questions.question: How can you reduce hydroplaning risk?

options.text: Do not speed on wet roads.
Keep tires at the correct air pressure.
Replace worn tires.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your vehicle slides on water between the tires and road. Low tire pressure and worn tread increase hydroplaning risk. Speeding also increases this risk.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing with flashing signals, you should:

options.text: Stop and look for a train.
Slow down and look for a train.
Look for a train, then speed up.
Do what the vehicle ahead does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and look for a train.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing signals at a railroad crossing, you must stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail. Watch for other warning signs like lowered gates or the sound of an approaching train.

questions.question: You may cross a dashed white line:

options.text: At any time.
Only during daylight hours.
When it is safe to change lanes.
Only when passing a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it is safe to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Dashed white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. You may cross them to pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: You may drive around or under a lowering or raising railroad gate:

options.text: As long as a train is not too close.
If your vehicle can do so without damaging the gate.
If you look carefully in both directions first.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights, lowered gates, and bells at a railroad crossing mean you must stop completely. Wait until the lights and bells stop and the gates are fully up before crossing. Never drive around or under a moving gate.
